transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name], and I'll be speaking with you today. Can you tell me what brings you in?

Well, I guess I came in because I just feel… wound up, most of the day. Like my body is bracing for something, even when nothing is happening. I’ll be sitting at my computer, just doing normal work stuff, and I notice I’m all tense, like I’m waiting for some problem to pop up. 

And then even after dinner, when I’m supposed to be relaxing, it’s still there. It’s funny, my husband can just sit and watch a show and completely unwind, and I’ll be sitting there feeling like I should be doing something or preparing for something. I don’t know… it’s not unbearable, but it’s been enough that I thought I should come talk to someone.

Can you tell me if this feeling of being wound up has been happening even during times when things are going smoothly in your life, or does it seem to come up only when something stressful is going on?

It happens even when things are going fine, yeah. Like, I can be having a totally normal workday—nothing dramatic, just emails and spreadsheets and whatever—and I’ll still notice I’m sitting there all tight, like I’m bracing for something.

And after dinner too, which is odd because that should be the easy part of the day. My husband will be relaxed, watching TV, and I’m kind of perched there like there’s something I forgot to do. It’s not only when there’s an actual crisis or anything.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when there isn’t an obvious problem?

Yes… yes, I do. It kind of jumps around. Like I’ll start thinking about my sister in Arecibo and whether she’s okay, and then suddenly I’m thinking, did I miss something at the office, some email I forgot to answer or a number I entered wrong.

And then if my husband is driving home, I’ll be watching the time even though he’s usually fine. Or I’ll remember something for church that I said I’d help with, and then bills pop into my head. It’s like my mind is preparing for problems that haven’t even happened. I don’t know why it does that.
Do you often feel restless, fatigued, or have muscle tension, especially when you’re not actively stressed about a specific problem?

Yeah, mostly the restless and tense part. I mean, I feel wound up a lot of the day, like my body is waiting for something to go wrong, even when I’m just sitting at my computer doing ordinary work.

And then at night after dinner, when I should be relaxing, I still feel kind of braced. My husband can just sit there and watch TV, and I’m sitting there like… I don’t know, like I should be getting ready for something. It’s not always tied to one specific problem.
Do you find it hard to control these worries, even when you know they might not make sense or aren’t likely to happen?

Yes… I do. I’ll even tell myself, “Daniela, enough, focus on this report,” and for a minute I think I’ve got it under control.

But then one little thought turns into five more. Like I’ll check one message just to make sure, and then I’m checking another thing, or replaying what could go wrong, and suddenly half an hour has gone by. It’s frustrating because part of me knows I’m probably making too much of it, but that doesn’t always make it stop.
Have you noticed any days where you feel down or hopeless, or where you lose interest in things you usually enjoy, even for a little while?

I don’t know… I mean, I wouldn’t say hopeless exactly. Maybe I get tired of my own head sometimes, but that’s different, right?

I still like the things I like. If anything, I get distracted from them. Like I’ll start making coffee and think, oh, I should call my sister, and then I remember the plant by the window needs water—my mother used to keep all these plants, she had a whole routine for them—and then I’ve forgotten what I was doing.

But feeling really down or not caring about anything… I haven’t really noticed that, no.
Do you find yourself getting irritable or more easily annoyed lately, especially when you're feeling this tension or worry?

Yes, a little. I’m usually pretty patient, or I try to be, anyway, but lately I notice these small things get under my skin faster than they should.

Like at work, if we’re in a documentation meeting and someone’s late with an update, I can feel myself getting tight and I answer more sharply than I mean to. Or at choir—this sounds so petty—but if someone is singing just a bit off-tempo, I get annoyed, and then I feel bad because it’s choir, it’s supposed to be enjoyable.

And Sundays too, when I’m cooking and everyone starts asking me questions at once, I’ll snap a little. Not yelling, exactly, just… sharper. Then afterward I think, why did I say it like that?
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, even when you’re not actively thinking about things?

Yes… mostly it’s the staying asleep part. I usually do fall asleep eventually, though sometimes I sort of putter around too long before bed—checking the kitchen, making sure the window’s closed, that kind of thing.

But then I wake up around three or four in the morning, and my brain just starts up. I’ll think about my sister’s next appointment, or some server issue at work, and then I’m lying there trying not to look at the clock because that makes it worse.

Even if I technically get enough hours, I wake up feeling like I didn’t really rest. Like I was asleep, but not in a useful way, if that makes sense.
Have you ever had sudden episodes where your heart races, you feel short of breath, or you experience intense fear that comes out of nowhere?

I don’t think so… not like out of nowhere. I mean, I’ve had moments where I feel wound up, but sudden intense fear with my heart racing and not being able to breathe—no, I wouldn’t really describe it that way.

Sometimes I wonder if I’m just bad at naming these things. My husband will say, “You seem tense,” and I’ll be like, “No, I’m just trying to remember if I sent that email,” and then somehow I’m reorganizing a drawer. But those big sudden episodes you’re describing… I haven’t noticed that.
Have these feelings of worry and tension been affecting your ability to function normally at work, home, or in social situations?

I mean… mostly I’m still functioning. I’m going to work, I’m getting the reports done, I’m there for my family, and I still go to church and choir and all that.

But it’s not as smooth as it used to be. At work, reports that should be fairly routine take me longer because I keep going back to check them—sometimes more than once. And then I’ll get distracted by some tiny formatting thing, which is ridiculous because nobody cares if the spacing is perfect, but I’ll still fuss with it.

At home, I’m showing up, but I’ve had to apologize a few times because I sounded short with people. Not anything dramatic, just… my tone comes out sharper than I intend. Then I feel bad about it later. So yes, I’m managing, but it’s taking more effort than it used to.
